problem_statement:
Ship preflight lets a second `npm run ship` start on the same checkout

On 2026-09-24 two ships were started about 13 seconds apart on one checkout. Both passed the preflight step ("nothing else holding the tree"), their react-router builds wrote into the same `build/` directory, and one wiped the other's client manifest mid-build. One ship refused late at step 8; the other deployed.

The preflight already scans the process table (`busyProcesses` in `scripts/lib/child-processes.mjs`, using the `SHIP_BUSY_NEEDLES` list) and refuses while a gate run or an orphaned preview server is alive, but it does not treat another running ship as busy.

To reproduce: build a process table containing two ship process trees (npm -> `cmd /d /s /c node scripts/ship.mjs` -> `node scripts/ship.mjs` tee parent -> the ship child) and call `busyProcesses(table, SHIP_BUSY_NEEDLES, <pid of one ship child>)`. Nothing is reported.

Expected:
- the other ship's processes whose command line runs `scripts/ship.mjs` are reported, each described as "another ship";
- the running ship must not flag itself: its own launchers (its parent shell, its tee parent, i.e. its whole ancestor chain) are excused along with its own pid, so a lone ship still passes its own preflight;
- a parentage cycle caused by reused pids must not hang the scan.
fail_to_pass: node --test --test-name-pattern="a second ship is found" test/ship-preflight.test.mjs
pass_to_pass: node --test --test-name-pattern="a lone ship passes its own preflight" test/ship-preflight.test.mjs
